drafts.title: Let customers view, export and delete their driver profile data from the vehicle or companion app
drafts.description: Customers can inspect what data is stored in their driver profile, export a copy, and delete their profile data directly from the vehicle or the BMW companion app without contacting support.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A customer can (1) view a summary of stored profile data, (2) export a machine-readable copy, and (3) permanently delete their driver profile from vehicle and cloud within 24 hours; tests with 20 pilot users show successful export/delete in 95% of attempts.
assumptions: Vehicle has secure authenticated owner account linking to cloud profile.
Backend supports export and deletion APIs; deletion propagates to vehicle within 24 hours.
uncertainties: Exact legal retention windows in certain markets may require retention beyond a user's deletion request; legal exceptions could affect UX.
Export format expectations (fields customers expect) must be validated with user testing.

drafts.title: Voice control reliably understands simple driving commands
drafts.description: While driving, customers can speak common commands (navigation, media, climate prompts) and expect the system to correctly carry them out without repeating or manual correction.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In real-world driving noise tests across highways and city streets, the voice system correctly executes 95% of a 100-item set of common driving commands (play music, set temp to 21°C/70°F, call contact X, navigate to address) without requiring repetition.
assumptions: Training will include in-cabin noise profiles and diverse accents typical for the US market.
Onboard and cloud models can update iteratively after launch.
uncertainties: Performance may vary with non-standard accents, heavy background conversation, or aftermarket window tinting affecting cabin acoustics.

drafts.title: Wireless phone charging that maintains charge without dropouts during drives
drafts.description: Customers can rely on the wireless charging pad to keep their phone charging throughout normal trips without frequent interruptions; when wireless fails, they have clear fallback guidance.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across a test matrix of the 20 most popular phone models (with typical cases) the wireless pad maintains continuous charging for 2-hour driving sessions in 95% of sessions; when charging stops, the vehicle UI shows a clear notification and suggested fixes (alignment, case removal) within 5 seconds.
assumptions: Tests assume typical protective phone cases (up to 3 mm) and common phone sizes.
Firmware updates to the charger and companion app are available to diagnose interruptions.
uncertainties: Some phone models or cases may never reliably charge wirelessly; compatibility matrix will need maintenance.

drafts.title: Head-up and center displays remain readable in bright sunlight and reduce glare
drafts.description: Drivers can read key information on the HUD (speed, navigation prompts) and the center screen under bright sunlight without needing to shade the display or move their head.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In controlled tests with direct sunlight (~50,000 lux) and typical driver seating positions, 95% of participants can read HUD speed and next navigation cue within 1.5 seconds and can correctly identify a center-screen critical menu item within 2.5 seconds.
assumptions: Improvements may combine higher display luminance, adaptive brightness, anti-reflective coatings, and UI contrast tuning.
Test lighting levels approximate typical midday sun with reflections through windshield.
uncertainties: Extreme aftermarket windshield tints or reflective dashboard accessories may reduce effectiveness.
Absolute lux thresholds may vary by geographic market and season.

drafts.title: Physical, tactile climate controls for temperature and fan speed that can be used without looking
drafts.description: Customers can adjust temperature and fan speed by touch while keeping their eyes on the road—controls provide clear tactile differentiation and immediate feedback.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In blind-touch tests (drivers keeping eyes forward), 95% of participants correctly change temperature by ±2°C (or ±4°F) and change fan speed by at least two steps within 2 seconds using tactile controls.
assumptions: Tactile elements will be distinguishable by feel and integrate with the cabin aesthetic.
Audio or haptic confirmation may be used as secondary feedback.
uncertainties: Some customers prefer minimal physical controls for a clean interior; final layout must balance aesthetics with usability.

drafts.title: Allow heated seats to be enabled and managed as a subscription/feature toggle (no mandatory hardware changes for customers who already have seats)
drafts.description: Customers who prefer a pay-for-use model can activate heated seats via a subscription or temporary activation in their account; the vehicle UI shows subscription status and allows enabling/disabling without dealership visit.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A customer can purchase and enable a heated-seats subscription via the app or in-car UI and have the feature active in the vehicle within 24 hours in 95% of trials; the UI shows current subscription status and remaining active period.
assumptions: Backend subscription systems and vehicle entitlement checks are available at launch.
Heated-seat hardware is present in the vehicle; subscription controls only toggle access to hardware.
uncertainties: Regulatory or market rules in some countries may limit pay-per-function activations; availability may vary by market.

drafts.title: Include the heated steering wheel as part of the Cold Weather package (so it is not sold only as an expensive standalone option)
drafts.description: US customers who select the Cold Weather package receive the heated steering wheel by default rather than needing to add it separately as an expensive option.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For all US-configured trims where a Cold Weather package is offered, the package configuration includes a heated steering wheel in 100% of published package contents at launch.
assumptions: Package contents can be adjusted in the configurator and build options prior to production decisions.
Inclusion does not mandate changing pricing in this requirement (pricing strategy handled separately).
uncertainties: Some high-performance or very low-cost trims may require different packaging decisions; exceptions should be documented.

drafts.title: Request to pass China CCC certification (regulatory ask) — out of scope for product requirements
drafts.description: Customers ask that the infotainment system pass China Compulsory Certification (CCC) for the Chinese market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: regulatory certification request recorded for regional compliance and market launch planning.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory certification/homologation requests are out of scope for product requirement drafting; record for compliance and market launch teams.

drafts.title: Request for a specific cockpit chip (Snapdragon 8295) — engineering specification out of scope
drafts.description: Customers asked that the cockpit computer use the Snapdragon 8295 chip.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: specific hardware part requests are engineering specifications and will be evaluated by architecture and hardware teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Requests for specific chips or component part numbers are engineering specifications and out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Requests about base price, lease rates, package discounts, dealer margins and financing offers — price/finance items out of scope
drafts.description: Customers requested lower base price, cheaper lease, free included packages, 30% Comfort-package discount, lower dealer margin on extras, and 0% financing offers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: pricing, lease rates, discounts, dealer margin and financing requests are commercial decisions and not product functional requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Price, lease, discount and financing requests are out of scope for product requirement drafting; pass to commercial/pricing teams.
